thread:
emily: Quick follow-up from the gateway RFC: staging repro shows hedged requests can both commit when an upstream closes mid-stream. We saw duplicate billing.
zack: Yikes. Is it hedging or resume semantics?
emily: Both. Edge A saw EOF and finalized; Edge B (hedged path) got more tokens and also finalized.
rachel: Short fix idea: on EOF-without-trailer, delay final commit by a small grace window (configurable per route).
tom: We should add a resume-seq header from runtime (x-resume-seq) and require hedged path to present > last_committed_seq.
emily: Also change billing finalize to CAS on (tenant, req_id, commit_seq) so duplicates are detected.
zack: Metrics/alerts: duplicate_billing_count per-tenant, hedge_rejects.
infra-bot: Canary deploy window requested: 04:00-06:00 UTC. Add rollback runbook if duplicates spike.
emily: I'll open an RFC with config schema (hedging.grace_ms), runtime contract for x-resume-seq, billing CAS API, and a small fuzz harness.
